classification.difficultyReason: Infer the intersection from the total and overlapping counts, then restrict the denominator to each given event.

content.prompt:
A group of 12 people met at a café for lunch. Everyone had a pie or chips or both.
If 9 people had a pie and 7 had chips, find the probability that one of the people:

children.label: a
children.prompt: had chips, given that this person had a pie

answer.worked:
A Venn diagram is useful here. Let $P$ be the set of people who had a pie and $C$ the set who had chips.
$$\begin{align*}|P\cap C|&=9+7-12\\|P\cap C|&=4\\P(C\mid P)&=\frac{|P\cap C|}{|P|}\\P(C\mid P)&=\frac{4}{9}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: did not have a pie given that the person had chips.

answer.worked:
There are $9+7-12=4$ people who had both a pie and chips.
$$\begin{align*}|P'\cap C|&=7-4\\|P'\cap C|&=3\\P(P'\mid C)&=\frac{|P'\cap C|}{|C|}\\P(P'\mid C)&=\frac{3}{7}\end{align*}$$
